title: Anthropic STEM Fellow
location: Remote-Friendly, United States; San Francisco, CA
description:
About Anthropic
 Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
 Program Overview
 Some of our world's grand challenges, from resolving long-open problems in mathematics to designing medicines for neglected diseases, require deep expert judgment that today's AI still lacks. We're working toward an AI scientist, a system capable of the long-horizon reasoning and experimental judgment needed to push the frontier on problems like these. We believe frontier AI, developed safely, can meaningfully accelerate progress across science and engineering. Getting there requires close collaboration with people who have spent years at the frontier of their fields.
 The Anthropic STEM Fellows Program brings researchers and experts from across science and engineering into Anthropic for four months to take on the grand challenges of their fields with Claude. Working in small pods of Fellows from related fields, you will pair deep domain expertise with our frontier models and internal tooling to define the hardest open problems in your discipline, build the datasets and simulations that let us test and train Claude on them, and find exactly where it falls short.
 We're looking for Fellows across science and engineering. Prior machine learning experience is helpful but not required. Scientific judgment and a willingness to learn quickly matter more.
 Our first cohort of more than 20 STEM Fellows across mathematics, physics, the life sciences, and engineering, ran from June to September 2026. The problems they built now feed Claude's training and one of our internal science evaluations.

title: Head of Strategic Partnerships, Global Systems Integrators
description:
About Scale AI
 Our mission is to develop reliable AI systems for the world's most important decisions. The Enterprise AI business delivers performant, reliable, and production-grade AI applications to enterprises across all industries by providing Generative AI expertise and infrastructure.
 The Role

This leader will build high-impact relationships with world-class partners, focused on professional services firms, to accelerate the development of AI applications with Scale.
 We are looking for a revenue-minded leader to own GSI-sourced and GSI-influenced pipeline. You should be able to set the strategy and also run the operating cadence it takes to turn alliance agreements into closed revenue: joint account plans, co-sell motions, practice building, and delivery enablement. You will source, evaluate, negotiate, and execute partnerships covering go-to-market, joint solutions, and delivery areas.
 This is a highly cross-functional role, as you will collaborate across internal teams including product, engineering, finance, legal, marketing and operations.

title: Senior Scientific Software Engineer — Simulation and Machine Learning
description:
Location: Remote within Europe, with regular presence in Bremen

Direct Reports: None; supervision of students and interns

Working Model: Remote / hybrid. Regular time on-site in Bremen.

Mission

Build the simulation and model-learning engine at the centre of Constructor's quantum software. The work is numerics-heavy: differentiable simulation of physical systems, inference of model parameters from experimental data, and optimisation at scale. The role sits between physics and engineering and requires genuine depth in both.

Responsibilities

Pillar 1 Simulation Engine

  • Build and maintain high-performance simulation code for open and closed quantum systems.
  • Own the differentiable simulation and automatic differentiation layer.
  • Drive performance. This code runs inside optimisation loops and speed decides what is possible.
  • Maintain and extend the Julia core and its Python interface.

Success Metrics and KPIs: simulation accuracy against measurement, runtime performance, API stability.

Pillar 2 Model Learning and Optimisation

  • Implement parameter inference and model learning from experimental data.
  • Work on neural-network approaches to PDE solving and equation discovery.
  • Benchmark against established academic tools and publish the comparison.

Success Metrics and KPIs: benchmark results, methods adopted by the research group, publications.

Pillar 3 Research Collaboration

  • Work with Constructor University faculty on joint research and grant applications.
  • Supervise graduate students and interns working on the engine.
  • Contribute to course material on numerical simulation and machine learning for physics.

Accountability: research collaborations initiat…

title: Senior Frontend Engineer — Scientific Applications
description:
Location: Remote within Europe, with regular presence in Bremen

Direct Reports: None

Working Model: Remote / hybrid. Regular time on-site in Bremen.

Mission

Own the interface layer for a scientific platform used by research teams to run complex physical experiments. The work is heavier than typical product frontend — live experiment monitoring, workflow graphs, large result sets, and users who are physicists rather than consumers. The Senior Frontend Engineer owns that layer end to end and sets the standard for it.

Responsibilities

Pillar 1 Frontend Ownership

  • Own the architecture, code and standards for the platform frontend.
  • Build and maintain complex interactive visualisation: directed workflow graphs, live monitoring, large-scale result inspection.
  • Handle long-running asynchronous work properly — progress, failure states, partial results.
  • Lead the migration to the Constructor React component library.

Success Metrics and KPIs: interface stability, adoption by the research team, migration delivered.

Pillar 2 Quality and Practice

  • Bring test coverage and review discipline to a codebase built at research pace.
  • Establish component standards and a shared design language with the wider Constructor frontend group.
  • Reach into the backend when that is what unblocks the work.

Success Metrics and KPIs: test coverage, defects reaching users, review turnaround.

Pillar 3 Working with Scientists

  • Work directly with the physicists who use the interface. Understand the experiment, not just the ticket.
  • Turn vague scientific requirements into concrete interface decisions.

Accountability: researchers able to run and monitor experiments without asking for help…
